claims.text: Thin pools hit long-tail LSTs hardest. Sanctum says it supports over 1,300 LSTs and that a well-supported LST can trade within a fraction of a percent of fair value while a smaller LST with limited DEX liquidity and no shared liquidity layer can see much wider spreads in volatile periods. Sanctum says price impact on shallow-reserve LSTs can spike even at modest sizes, and that delayed unstake avoids pool liquidity entirely. This is a vendor statement. (low confidence)

In the SPL stake-pool program, withdraw-sol pays from the pool's reserve and fails if the reserve holds too little SOL (normal when the manager has staked all of it). Withdraw-stake always works unless the user's pool-token account is frozen, but it returns an active stake account, so the holder must deactivate it and wait for the epoch boundary. Withdrawal order for stake: preferred validator, any validator, transient, reserve, then removing a validator account. (low confidence)

When an issuer's own frontend is gone, third-party routes can still convert the LST. In the Lido case, a Sanctum team member told DL News that holders could trade stSOL for SOL or other LSTs through Sanctum, Cointelegraph noted users pointing to Sanctum or Jupiter, and a Marinade contributor told SolanaFloor the Marinade app can redelegate any stake account or LST instantly. SolanaFloor is a subsidiary of Jito Network, a Marinade competitor, and the Marinade statement is the contributor's own. (medium confidence)

To pick an exit, compare the all-in quote of each route, because the best route flips with size and liquidity. Marinade and Sanctum both tell users to compare the Receive amount: instant wins at small sizes and deep liquidity, and delayed wins when spreads widen or orders are large. Sanctum suggests splitting a large position: instant-unstake what is needed now and delayed-unstake the rest. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Marinade's help centre lists mSOL Delayed Unstake at a 0.2% protocol fee with a 1.0043 SOL minimum. Instant Unstake carries no Marinade fee: it is a DEX swap, so the cost is spread and price impact, usually under 0.2% with deep liquidity. Both help pages give this; the pages show no effective date. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Marinade charges mSOL holders a flat 0.2% protocol fee on Delayed Unstake, with a 1.0043 SOL minimum, deducted before the ticket is credited. Instant Unstake of mSOL has no Marinade fee: it routes through DEXes, so the cost is spread and slippage. Marinade says Instant usually returns more SOL when mSOL liquidity is deep, and Delayed wins when many people unstake at once and spreads widen. The app shows both quotes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

In the SPL stake-pool program, withdraw-sol pays from the pool reserve and fails when the reserve holds too little SOL, which is normal when the manager has staked everything. Withdraw-stake returns an active stake account and works unless the user's pool-token account is frozen, so a holder can always exit but must then deactivate the stake and wait for the epoch boundary. Withdrawals draw from, in order: the preferred validator account, other validator accounts, transient accounts, then the reserve. A client that tries the reserve too early gets the program log 'Error withdrawing from reserve: validator stake accounts have lamports available, please use those first.' (medium confidence)

Kamino now prices all its LSTs at the stake rate read on chain (SOL staked / LST minted), not at the DEX price, so a DEX depeg does not trigger liquidations. Kamino argues a market-price oracle would turn every brief depeg into a cascade, because liquidations add selling, which deepens the depeg, which causes more liquidations; it singles out leveraged Multiply loops. The cost: stake-rate pricing does not cover a fundamental depeg, and it assumes arbitrage restores the market price. If unstaking is blocked and a depeg persists, the protocol could hold collateral worth more on paper than the market pays, and bad debt is socialised among lenders. Kamino lists supply caps, an asset-risk review of each LST's smart contract risk, and monitoring of stake pool health and unstaking delays as mitigations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

For native stake, Marinade sells whole stake accounts to buyers. An approved buyer pays SOL in the same transaction (atomic swap), or the stake sits on offer as a limit order until it sells. Marinade built this with Anza and calls it a request-for-quote market. Typical cost on Marinade Native and Select is 0.10%-0.40%, including a 0.01% protocol fee and about 0.00097 SOL of one-time listing rent. Eligibility: stake accounts of 1 SOL or more that are not activating or deactivating. Marinade warns that capacity is never guaranteed and large positions may need to be unstaked in portions. Delayed Unstake for native stake is a flat 0.003 SOL charged from the wallet. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Marinade's help article says that for mSOL a delayed-unstake request made in the last 2 hours of an epoch is pushed back one epoch (up to about 2 days); native stake accounts have no cut-off. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Lenders priced mSOL differently, so the same DEX dip liquidated some users and not others. SolanaFloor says liquidations hit Kamino and Marginfi (scale unclear) and that Solend said its system does not use LST depegs for liquidation. Solana Compass's AI-generated episode notes (which say they may be inaccurate) report that Marginfi prices every asset at market with a one-hour EMA, and that Solend prices mSOL with the SOL oracle, citing 31 price quoters for SOL against 14 for mSOL. (medium confidence)
